# ENFORCED conflict boundaries for the 'cpu-text' environment.

# are not documentation. Every one is also asserted against requirements.lock by
# `latence env verify`, so a boundary that stops holding fails the build.

# THE gliner2 MAJOR BOUNDARY (ADR-0064). gliner2 2.0.0 was released 2026-08-24, and it is a genuine major: the GLiNER 2.5 checkpoints are the new `boundary` architecture head, every 1.x checkpoint is `span`, and AutoExtractor.from_pretrained refuses to convert between them ("Span and boundary heads are not checkpoint-compatible"). This environment installs the 1.x Providers (latence-extract-gliner2 / latence-pii-gliner2, which declare gliner2[local]>=1.3,<2), so an unconstrained resolve is free to take a 2.x that their checkpoints cannot load. The cap ALSO makes the reverse impossible: latence-gliner25 declares gliner2[local]>=2.0,<3, which is disjoint from this window, so adding it to workspace_packages fails `latence env verify` with E-CONSTRAINT-CONFLICT — offline, on every commit, at dependency-resolution time rather than at model load on a pod. One resolved environment holds ONE gliner2 major; the 2.5 Providers belong to an environment that resolves the 2.x line.
gliner2>=1.3,<2

# THE binding conflict of this stack. Floor: gliner 0.2.27 (the learned PII Provider's engine) declares transformers>=4.51.3. Cap: latence-disambig-glinker declares transformers<5 because glinker 0.1.1 and flashdeberta 0.0.7 are written against the transformers 4.x API. The latest transformers on PyPI is 5.14.1, so an UNCONSTRAINED install lands a 5.x and breaks GLinker at import. The only viable window is 4.51.3 <= v < 5.
transformers>=4.51.3,<5

# transformers 4.57.6 declares huggingface-hub>=0.34.0,<1.0, while the latest hub release is 1.24.0. Unconstrained, the resolver is free to take a 1.x that transformers 4.x cannot use. Also satisfies latence-disambig-glinker's own >=0.23,<1 cap.
huggingface-hub>=0.34,<1

# transformers 4.57.6 declares tokenizers>=0.22.0,<=0.23.0 and the latest tokenizers release is 0.23.1 — one patch outside the window. This is the classic silent-drift failure: nothing in the framework mentions tokenizers, yet an unpinned resolve can break the whole stack.
tokenizers>=0.22,<=0.23.0

# The cap latence-disambig-glinker declares (a torch major break would ABI-break the prebuilt flashdeberta/triton wheels this stack depends on). The lock additionally pins the `+cpu` local version from the PyTorch CPU index so no CUDA payload enters a CPU environment.
torch>=2.1,<3
